title: Biocon's Pertuzumab Biosimilar Pebrilzo Gets European Commission Marketing Authorisation
summary: New Delhi: Biocon Limited has announced that the European Commission (EC) has granted marketing authorization for Pebrilzo, its biosimilar pertuzumab, for the treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer...

contentHtml:
New Delhi: Biocon Limited has announced that the European Commission (EC) has granted marketing authorization for Pebrilzo, its biosimilar pertuzumab, for the treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer across multiple disease stages in the European Union (EU).

Biocon’s pertuzumab biosimilar is the first biosimilar to receive EC marketing authorisation under the European Medicines Agency’s (EMA) new tailored clinical approach. This milestone follows its positive CHMP opinion on September 17, 2026.

Shreehas Tambe, CEO & Managing Director, Biocon, said: “The European Commission’s approval of Pebrilzo®, our pertuzumab biosimilar, the first under its new tailored clinical pathway, marks a significant regulatory milestone for Biocon. With this approval, pertuzumab becomes our fifth oncology biosimilar approved in both Europe and the United States, strengthening our global oncology portfolio and reinforcing our commitment to expanding access to high-quality, affordable biologic therapies for patients with HER2-positive breast cancer.”

Molecule Information: Biocon’s pertuzumab biosimilar, approved as a 420 mg concentrate for solution for infusion, is a biosimilar medicinal product and the active substance is pertuzumab, a monoclonal antibody that binds with high affinity and specificity to the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), inhibiting the proliferation of tumour cells that overexpress HER2.

Biocon’s pertuzumab biosimilar is indicated for use in combination with trastuzumab and chemotherapy in the neoadjuvant treatment of adult patients with HER2-positive, locally advanced, inflammatory, or early-stage breast cancer at high risk of recurrence, as well as in the adjuvant treatment of adult patients with HER2-positive early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence.

In addition, it is indicated for use in combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel in adult patients with HER2 positive metastatic or locally recurrent unresectable breast cancer, who have not received previous anti-HER2 therapy or chemotherapy for their metastatic disease.

Extensive orthogonal, state-of-the-art structural and functional analytical characterisation, together with comparative clinical pharmacokinetic data, demonstrated that Biocon’s pertuzumab biosimilar is highly similar to the reference product, with no clinically meaningful differences in quality, safety, or efficacy.

Biocon has a strong and growing commitment to oncology, with a portfolio spanning multiple areas of cancer care, including solid tumors such as breast cancer, as well as supportive care addressing chemotherapy-induced neutropenia. This commitment also extends to bone health, with therapies addressing osteoporosis, treatment-related bone loss and skeletal complications associated with advanced cancers1. Biosimilar pertuzumab further strengthens the company’s portfolio and its ability to support patients across different stages of the cancer care journey and diverse healthcare systems.

Breast cancer remains the most commonly diagnosed cancer among women in Europe. According to 2024 estimates from the European Cancer Information System (ECIS), it is the leading cancer diagnosis among women across Europe2. Approximately 15–20% of invasive breast cancers are characterised by HER2 overexpression or amplification3.Despite significant advances in HER2-targeted treatment, the burden of breast cancer underscores the importance of broad and sustainable access to high-quality treatment options across European healthcare systems.2,3.

Biocon Limited is a global biopharmaceutical company driven by its purpose to provide affordable, life-changing medicines to patients worldwide. Headquartered in Bengaluru, India, Biocon addresses some of the world’s most pressing healthcare challenges across chronic and non-communicable diseases by offering both biosimilars and generics at scale across geographies. Through this diversified portfolio, Biocon focuses on areas of high unmet need, spanning key therapy areas including diabetes, oncology, obesity, cardiovascular diseases, immunology, ophthalmology, and bone health. The company has pioneered several industry firsts that have helped shape the global biosimilars landscape.

To date, the company has commercialized 12 biosimilar products and 30+ generic formulations globally. It has robust research and development pipeline of 20+ biosimilar assets, as well as GLP-1 peptides and other complex generics. With an integrated lab-to-patient model, Biocon brings together research and development, manufacturing, and commercial capabilities to ensure reliable and scalable supply of medicines. The company operates in more than 120 countries, supported by seven manufacturing sites, three R&D sites, 18 offices worldwide, and a workforce of over 9,500 employees. Biocon has been included in the S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook 2026 for the fourth consecutive year, underscoring its commitment to sustainable and responsible growth.
